subject: Pilot SLO hypothesis, reserved throughput ask, and hardware shortlist
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: mike.chen@helioworks.com, ruth.hayes@helioworks.com
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 27 Mar 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + hypothesis for pilot (latency/throughput)

Mike / Ruth — thanks for the call today. Quick post-call recap so we’re aligned and can move to a short dedicated pilot: 

Call highlights (what we heard)
- Primary SLO: p95 latency ≤ 150 ms for text-complete responses (average prompt length ~120 tokens).
- Streaming: client expects incremental token flush every ~120 ms for first 1.5s of response to maintain UI feel.
- Concurrency profile: steady baseline ~80 concurrent active sessions, peak spikes up to 250 for bursts (10–15 min).
- Throughput target: steady-state equivalent of ~220 req/s (based on 3s average response token gen), bursts up to ~700 req/s for short windows.
- Model plan: HelioWorks will pilot with an open 13B variant (FP16) for Phase 1; potential to move to quantized 8-bit for cost optimization if quality holds.
- Security: must run Dedicated (no hosted multi-tenant) and support SOC2 audit artifacts.

Immediate ask from Redwood: we’d like to propose a short capacity validation pilot (7–10 days) that confirms:
1) GPU shortlist (H100-80GB, A100-40/80GB, and an L4-style inference node) tradeoffs for streaming latency and reserved throughput;
2) reserved throughput number to back your SLA (tokens/sec and concurrent allocations);
3) a smoke benchmark with representative prompt set and 95/99 latency curves.

Attached: SLO readout template (slo_readout_table.xlsx) and a one-page pilot proposal (redwood-pilot-proposal-helioworks.pdf).

Next steps I propose:
- Karthik & Vanessa to run a focused bench (3-day synthetic) on our side targeting your prompt lengths and burst pattern.
- Schedule a 30-min sync Thurs to review preliminary numbers and firm up reserved throughput for pricing.

Can you confirm the baseline throughput numbers above match your telemetry and any additional constraints (max sequence length, expected average output length)?

Thanks — Ben

Ben — good notes. A few clarifying questions / initial hypotheses from infra that we should capture before the smoke bench: 

Questions for HelioWorks
- When you say p95 ≤ 150 ms, is that server-to-client response completion (end-to-end), or p95 for each token flush during streaming? We need to know which metric we gate.
- Typical request token composition: prompt tokens vs generation tokens? (you gave ~120 prompt tokens — what’s the expected average gen tokens?)
- Any hard max sequence length to reserve memory for KV cache?
- Are you ok with a short soft-fail mode where we fallback to a smaller model variant if we see sustained queueing?

Bench plan notes (internal)
- For streaming-sensitive UI, H100 and A100 behave similarly on throughput for batch workloads, but H100 generally wins on short-sequence low-latency due to Tensor cores and larger HBM. L4-class cards are cheaper but may need more replicas to hit burst headroom.
- Reserve throughput should be expressed in tokens/sec (sustained) and an upper-burst cap for billing/guardrails. For initial pricing we should propose: sustain 220 req/s -> estimate ~XX tokens/sec (need Helio avg gen tokens) and burst headroom 3x.
- Test matrix: run single-query latency, 1–20 concurrent, 80–250 concurrent, and a 15-min burst at 700 req/s. Capture p50/p95/p99 and time-to-first-token.

Action items:
- Karthik: I’ll spin up bench VMs and draft HW-run matrix.
- Vanessa: please prep a preliminary cost delta table (H100 vs A100 vs L4 replicas) for Thurs.

I’ll start with conservative kernel configs and include a quantized run if model fidelity is acceptable.

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

- p95 comment: we expect p95 for end-to-end completion (not per-token). For streaming quality we also want 1st token < 120 ms for interactive flows (mobile clients).
- Average generated tokens: 180 tokens (so prompt ~120 + gen ~180 -> ~300 token round-trip typical).
- Max sequence length: we may hit up to 1024 in some complex queries, but 512 will cover ~90% initially.
- Security: must be Dedicated. SOC2 evidence needed but we can share narrower artifact set for pilot.
- Pricing ask: can you provide a tentative reserved throughput quote (sustained 220 req/s; burst up to 700 req/s) and suggested SLAs? Pricing will determine whether we move forward quickly.

Also: during call we noted a UI requirement — partial flush every ~120 ms for first 1.5s. If you can validate time-to-first-token and time-between-token-chunks in the bench that would be great.

Happy to run a small sample dataset for you if that helps tune the bench.

Thanks Mike — this is perfect and helps finalize the bench. Final confirmation and proposed next steps: 

Bench inputs (confirmed)
- prompt tokens: ~120; gen tokens: ~180 -> mean ~300 tokens per request.
- max seq to account for: 1024 (we’ll include a 90/10 split in the bench).
- streaming: target TTF < 120 ms and token-chunk cadence ~120 ms for first 1.5s.
- concurrency: baseline 80, burst 250, pricing runway for 700 req/s spikes.

Preliminary HW shortlist (for pilot):
- H100-80GB (1–2 replicas): best single-rep latency for short sequences; higher cost but likely fewer nodes.
- A100-80GB (2–3 replicas): good balance for batchy bursts; proven latency at scale.
- L4-class inference (3–6 replicas): lower cost per-card, needs more replicas to match burst headroom — may be good for cost-constrained lanes.

We’ll run the following pilot cadence (7 business days):
Day 0–1: baseline smoke tests (single-query, up to 20 concurrent)
Day 2–4: steady-state sustained run at 220 req/s (capture p50/p95/p99)
Day 5: 15-min burst to 700 req/s, observe queueing/fallbacks
Day 6: streaming-focused tests (TTF, token-chunk cadence)
Day 7: quantized run (8-bit) for cost comparison if fidelity acceptable

Deliverables: detailed latency/throughput matrix, recommended reserved throughput (tokens/sec and concurrency allocation), HW cost delta table, and a go/no-go recommendation for Reserved Capacity sizing.

Action items assigned:
- Karthik: run bench and upload results to the Drive link in 4 days.
- Vanessa: pricing delta table + preliminary reserved throughput quote by Thurs EOD.
- Mike / Ruth: share a short sample of 30 representative prompts (if possible) to reduce noise in bench.
- Ben: draft a short MPA (mutual pilot agreement) and a PO template for reserved throughput commitments.

Proposed meeting: Thurs 28 Mar 2028 10:00 AM PT — 30 min to review initial numbers. I’ll send a calendar invite once Vanessa posts the cost table.

Thanks all — Ben
